title: Why You Procrastinate (It's Not Laziness)
description: Procrastination is not a time-management problem. Here is what is really going on in your head, and a two-minute trick that helps you start.

scenes.say: You have something important to do. You know it matters. And yet, here you are, watching a stickman on the internet.
So why do we put things off, even when we know it will hurt us later?
Most people think the answer is laziness, or bad time management.
But researchers who study procrastination say that is not the real cause.
Procrastination is mostly about feelings. The task makes you feel bored, anxious, or not good enough.
So your brain looks for a quick escape. And your phone is always happy to help.
You feel better for a moment. But the task is still there, and now you also feel guilty.
That guilt makes the task feel even worse, so you avoid it again. It becomes a loop.
Here is a simple way to break it. It is called the two minute rule.
Do not promise to finish the task. Only promise to work on it for two minutes.
Open the document. Write one sentence. Put on your running shoes.
Starting is the hardest part. Once you begin, the bad feeling fades, and continuing gets much easier.
And if you still stop after two minutes? That is fine. You did more than zero.
So pick the one thing you have been avoiding, and give it two minutes right now. Then come back and subscribe.

short.title: You're not lazy. Try the 2-minute rule #shorts

scenes.say: You are not lazy. You procrastinate for a different reason.
The task makes you feel bored or anxious, so your brain runs away to something easier.
The fix is the two minute rule. Only promise to work for two minutes.
Starting is the hardest part. After that, it gets easier to keep going.
Try it right now on the thing you have been avoiding.
